answer: Running 276 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the ember schedule in the walnut ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the falcon checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 1 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 33 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
